newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL short-term interbank eases due to liquidity.
newsitem.headline: KL short-term interbank eases due to liquidity.

text.p: Short-term interbank rates were lower as banks increased the funds in the short-term market ahead of two major festivals next month, dealers said on Thursday.

They said many banks were borrowing long-term and keeping the funds at the short-end in anticipation of further withdrawals for the Moslem Eid al-Fitr and Chinese Lunar New Year festivals in February.
An estimated three billion ringgit is expected to temporarily go out of the banking system during the twin celebrations, dealers said.
"The market is not very liquid, but there is a lot of funds at the short-end," said a dealer with a Malaysian bank.
He said many people had overborrowed for the festivals.
Another dealer said the drop in overnight to 5.7 percent on Wednesday was also causing a drop in the short-term rates.
He said this was the lowest level for the overnight rate in many months, below the central banks's perceived floor of 5.8/6.0 percent.
One-week money was at 6.7/7.0 percent against 7.20/30 on Wednesday, two-week at 7.10/20 against 7.20/30 and one-month at 7.25/30 against 7.30/35.
Three-month and six-month money were at 7.30/35 percent, against 7.35/38 previously.
